V. A CA may provide, through a kiosk at a public place, any service he chooses, since a kiosk is merely a channel of delivery.

Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: I, II, III and V only
questions.explanation: Statements I, II and IV correctly reproduce the decisions: setting up a practice in an IFSC or GIFT city is permissible, as is rendering services to IFSC units from offices outside the IFSC; a CA firm may register itself on Udyog Aadhaar and a member may engage as a registration authority for obtaining digital signatures for clients; and two or more CAs may collectively take a joint GST training session for their clients and share the fees. Statement III is not correct because acting as authorised representative of a foreign company is permissible only provided the member is not the auditor of that company - the absence of assurance character in representation is not the condition the Board laid down. Statement V is not correct because provision of services through a kiosk is permissible only if the services provided are permitted for a practising CA, so the channel cannot validate an otherwise impermissible service. Any option which omits III or V, or which includes I, II or IV, misstates these conditional permissions.

questions.category: Recent Decisions of Ethical Standards Board - Directorships, Trusts and Societies
questions.question:
Consider the following situations of CA Vandana Rao, a member in practice:
P. She is appointed the auditor of the charitable trust of which she is already a member.
Q. She accepts the statutory audit of a society in which her spouse, a dependant, holds a position in the managing committee of the institutes governed by that society.
R. She advises a client on matters relating to its intellectual property rights.
S. She is engaged as the patent attorney of a client to appear before the patent registry.
T. Being a director simplicitor of a company, she signs ROC forms of that company.
U. She is appointed the statutory auditor of Converge Ltd, a joint venture of Ananya Ltd, of which she is a non-executive director.
V. Separately, she acts as an arbitrator in a commercial dispute between two companies with their consent.

Which of the above situations are NOT permissible for her?
options: P, R, T and U only
P, Q, S, T and U only
Q, S, T, U and V only
P, Q, S, T, U and V only
questions.explanation: P is barred because a CA who is a member of a trust cannot be the auditor of that trust; the Board draws the line at membership, which is why merely becoming the settlor of a trust is permissible. Q is barred because a CA cannot accept the statutory audit of a society where an immediate family member, that is a spouse or dependant, holds a position in the managing committee of the institutes governed by the society. S is barred because acting as a trademark or patent attorney is not permissible, although advice relating to intellectual property rights is, which makes R a permissible activity and excludes the options which list R. T is barred because a CA who is a director simplicitor cannot sign ROC forms of the company. U is barred because where a CA is a non-executive director in a company, he or his firm cannot accept appointment as statutory auditor of a company which is a joint venture of the original company, the impact on independence being the decisive consideration. V, being an arbitrator in court with the consent of parties, is expressly permissible, so the option which adds V is wrong.

questions.category: Recent Decisions of Ethical Standards Board - Research, Derivatives and Mystery Audit
questions.question: Case: CA Sameer Kulkarni, a member in practice, proposes five activities for FY 2025-26: (a) to act as an equity research adviser and to publish a retail research report carrying his firm's name; (b) to buy and sell derivative contracts for his own account; (c) to deal in commodity derivative contracts for his own account; (d) to accept a mystery audit assignment for a retail chain; (e) to undertake derivative transactions on behalf of his clients for a professional fee. Which combination of these activities is permissible for him?
questions.explanation: A member may become an equity research adviser, but the decisions add that he cannot publish a retail report, so (a) fails at the publication step even though the advisory role itself is permitted. A member may engage in derivative transactions in a personal capacity but not in a professional capacity for clients, so (b) is permissible and (e) is not. Activity (c) is separately barred, because a CA in practice cannot transact in commodity derivative transactions in any capacity, the words 'any capacity' overriding the personal capacity permission relied upon for (b). Activity (d) is permissible, acceptance of the assignment of mystery audit having been expressly cleared by the Board. The decisive distinction is therefore between securities derivatives dealt with personally, which is allowed, and commodity derivatives or client-borne dealing, which is not; options 0 and 1 retain one impermissible activity and option 2 retains two.

questions.category: Recent Decisions of Ethical Standards Board - Internal Audit and Provident Fund Work
questions.question:
Consider the following statements on the recent decisions of the Ethical Standards Board:
I. The internal auditor of the employees' provident fund trust of a government company may be appointed as the statutory auditor of that company.
II. A member may act as the internal auditor of a company and as the statutory auditor of that company's employees' provident fund trust, but not the other way round.
III. An internal auditor may accept appointment as the procurement officer of the same company, the two roles being complementary.
IV. The internal auditor of a company may purchase shares of that company, and may undertake the service assessment or performance audit of skill development council centres of the government.
V. An internal auditor may undertake the tax audit of the same company, provided the tax audit fee does not exceed his internal audit fee.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is not correct, because the internal auditor of the PF trust of a government company cannot be appointed as its statutory auditor. Statement II is correct and records the asymmetry which the Board permits: acting as internal auditor of a company and statutory auditor of its employees' PF fund is permissible, expressly not vice-versa. Statement III is not correct, because being appointed internal auditor and procurement officer simultaneously is impermissible, the procurement role involving decision-making on the very spends the internal auditor would examine. Statement IV is correct on both limbs, an internal auditor of a company being allowed to purchase shares of that company and service assessment or performance audit of skill development council centres of the government being permissible. Statement V is not correct, because an internal auditor shall not undertake tax audit or statutory audit, and vice-versa; the comparison of fees is borrowed from a different provision and creates no exception.

questions.category: Recent Decisions of Ethical Standards Board - CA in Service
questions.question: Case: CA Ritika Sen is a member of the Institute in employment as Deputy Finance Controller of Udupi Ceramics Ltd. Her employer's compliance committee considers four actions: (i) Ritika obtains an e-return registration and thereafter certifies the returns of the company filed through that registration; (ii) she appears before the GST authorities as the tax representative of Udupi Ceramics Ltd in a show-cause proceeding; (iii) she also agrees to appear as the tax representative of eleven individual employees of the company in their personal income-tax matters, against a fee; (iv) she performs her duties with due diligence and without gross negligence. Which combination of these actions is permissible?
questions.explanation: For a CA in service the decisions permit taking e-return registration if it does not conflict with his employment obligations, but expressly add that he cannot certify the return, so action (i) fails at the certification stage even though the registration itself could have been allowed. Action (ii) is the permitted half of the tax representative rule: a member in service may appear as a tax representative before tax authorities on behalf of his employer. Action (iii) is the prohibited half, because he may not appear on behalf of other employees of his employer, and the eleven clients are precisely such employees, whatever fee is charged. Action (iv) is unobjectionable and is the standard expected of a CA employee under Chapter II of the Council General Guidelines. Hence only (ii) and (iv) together form a fully permissible combination.

questions.category: Disciplinary Procedure - Routing of Complaint and Powers of the Forum
questions.question:
Case: On 10 January 2025 the Disciplinary Directorate receives, along with the prescribed fee, a complaint against CA Harish Pillai, a member in practice, alleging that while he was the statutory auditor of Vrinda Textiles Ltd he engaged in a compilation engagement as per SRS 4410 of that company and also exercised a lien over its records for his unpaid fees. The Directorate forms the opinion that Pillai is guilty, and it is common ground that the conduct complained of falls in both the First Schedule and the Second Schedule of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. On 2 February 2025 a second complaint is received alleging that Pillai's firm solicited clients by advertisement, a matter falling in the First Schedule, and on this the Directorate forms the opinion that he is not guilty; the matter is placed before the Board of Discipline, which on 15 September 2025 records its disagreement with that opinion. Pillai's counsel argues that the Directorate's opinion of 'not guilty' closes the second matter.

On the first complaint, which of the following correctly states the forum before which the matter must be placed and the punishment available to that forum if it finds him guilty?
options: Board of Discipline, because a complaint which touches the First Schedule is placed before it, and it may reprimand him, remove his name from the Register for up to 3 months or impose a fine up to ₹ 1 lac.

Disciplinary Committee, because a matter falling in the Second Schedule or in both schedules is placed before it, and it may reprimand him, remove his name from the Register for any time or permanently, or impose a fine up to ₹ 5 lacs.
Disciplinary Directorate itself, because having opined that the member is guilty it may reprimand him or impose a fine up to ₹ 5 lacs without reference to any other forum.
Appellate Authority, because where the conduct complained of falls in more than one schedule the complaint is tried in the first instance by that Authority.
questions.explanation: Where the Disciplinary Directorate opines that the CA is guilty, the routing depends on the schedule in which the matter falls: a First Schedule matter goes to the Board of Discipline, while a Second Schedule matter, or a matter falling in both schedules, goes to the Disciplinary Committee. Since the conduct here is agreed to fall in both schedules, the second limb governs and the matter must be placed before the Disciplinary Committee, which is why option 0, with the Board's comparatively limited powers of reprimand, removal of name up to 3 months and fine up to ₹ 1 lac, is the wrong forum as well as the wrong penalty. If the Committee finds him guilty it may reprimand him, remove his name for any time or permanently, or impose a fine up to ₹ 5 lacs, and if it finds him not guilty it closes the matter. The Directorate is not a punishing forum, so option 2 is wrong, and the Appellate Authority does not try complaints in the first instance, so option 3 is wrong.

questions.category: Disciplinary Procedure - Where the Board Disagrees with the Directorate
questions.question:
Case: On 10 January 2025 the Disciplinary Directorate receives, along with the prescribed fee, a complaint against CA Harish Pillai, a member in practice, alleging that while he was the statutory auditor of Vrinda Textiles Ltd he engaged in a compilation engagement as per SRS 4410 of that company and also exercised a lien over its records for his unpaid fees. The Directorate forms the opinion that Pillai is guilty, and it is common ground that the conduct complained of falls in both the First Schedule and the Second Schedule of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. On 2 February 2025 a second complaint is received alleging that Pillai's firm solicited clients by advertisement, a matter falling in the First Schedule, and on this the Directorate forms the opinion that he is not guilty; the matter is placed before the Board of Discipline, which on 15 September 2025 records its disagreement with that opinion. Pillai's counsel argues that the Directorate's opinion of 'not guilty' closes the second matter.

On the second complaint, which of the following is the correct position?
options: The Board must close the matter, because where the Directorate has once opined that the member is not guilty, the Board's only remaining option is to advise further investigation and it cannot itself enter into the complaint.

The Board must refer the matter to the Disciplinary Committee, because a complaint on which the Directorate and the Board differ can be decided by no other forum, whatever schedule the alleged misconduct falls in.

The Board may itself proceed with the matter and, if it finds him guilty, may remove his name from the Register for any period or permanently, or impose a fine up to ₹ 5 lacs, the Board being the forum which received the complaint.

The Board may advise the Directorate to further investigate, or may itself proceed with the matter because it relates to the First Schedule; if it finds him guilty it may reprimand him, remove his name for up to 3 months or impose a fine up to ₹ 1 lac, and an appeal against its order lies within 90 days to the Appellate Authority at the instance of the aggrieved member or of the Director (Discipline).
questions.explanation: An opinion of 'not guilty' by the Disciplinary Directorate does not close the matter; the matter is still placed before the Board of Discipline, and the counsel's argument is therefore wrong. Where the Board agrees with the Directorate it closes the matter, but where it disagrees it has three alternatives: to advise the Directorate to further investigate, to itself proceed with the matter if it relates to the First Schedule, or to refer the matter to the Disciplinary Committee if it relates to the Second Schedule or to both schedules. Since solicitation of clients by advertisement is a First Schedule matter, the Board may proceed with it, and the punishment at the Board's disposal is reprimand, removal of name for up to 3 months or a fine up to ₹ 1 lac, which makes option 2 wrong as to the penalty although right as to the forum. Referral to the Disciplinary Committee is reserved for Second Schedule or both-schedules matters, so option 1 overstates; option 0 wrongly treats further investigation as the only route. Any order of the Board is appealable within 90 days to the Appellate Authority by the aggrieved member or by the Director (Discipline).

questions.category: Disciplinary Procedure - Sequence from Complaint to Appeal
questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of steps in the disciplinary proceedings arising from a complaint against CA Harish Pillai, from receipt of the complaint up to the appellate stage?
options: Complaint with the prescribed fee received by the Disciplinary Directorate, which forms an opinion that the member is guilty or not guilty; if guilty, a First Schedule matter is placed before the Board of Discipline and a Second Schedule or both-schedules matter before the Disciplinary Committee, and if not guilty the matter is still placed before the Board of Discipline; the forum either finds him guilty and passes an order or finds him not guilty and closes the matter; an aggrieved member or the Director (Discipline) prefers an appeal within 90 days to the Appellate Authority.

Complaint with the prescribed fee received by the Disciplinary Directorate, which forms an opinion on guilt; if the opinion is 'not guilty' the matter is closed by the Directorate itself without reference to the Board of Discipline; if the opinion is 'guilty' the matter goes directly to the Appellate Authority, which tries the complaint in the first instance and passes an order appealable to the High Court.

Complaint with the prescribed fee received by the Board of Discipline, which frames the opinion on guilt in the first instance; whenever the Board differs from that opinion it must refer the matter to the Disciplinary Committee, whose powers are reprimand, removal of name for up to 3 months or a fine up to ₹ 1 lac, with an appeal lying within 60 days to the Appellate Authority.

Complaint with the prescribed fee received by the Disciplinary Directorate, which forms an opinion on guilt; if the opinion is 'guilty', First Schedule matters are referred to the Disciplinary Committee, which may reprimand, remove the name for up to 3 months or impose a fine up to ₹ 1 lac, and an appeal lies within 90 days to the Central Government.
questions.explanation: The flowchart begins with the Disciplinary Directorate receiving the complaint along with the fee and forming an opinion on guilt. If it opines that the CA is guilty, a First Schedule matter goes to the Board of Discipline, which may reprimand, remove the name for up to 3 months or impose a fine up to ₹ 1 lac, while a Second Schedule or both-schedules matter goes to the Disciplinary Committee, which may reprimand, remove the name for any time or permanently or impose a fine up to ₹ 5 lacs; if it opines that the CA is not guilty, the matter is nevertheless placed before the Board of Discipline, which may agree and close, advise further investigation, proceed itself on a First Schedule matter, or refer a Second Schedule or both-schedules matter to the Disciplinary Committee. The proceeding ends, on an order of the Board or the Committee, in an appeal within 90 days to the Appellate Authority by any member or the Director (Discipline) aggrieved. Option 1 wrongly lets the Directorate close a 'not guilty' matter itself; option 2 puts the complaint before the Board in the first instance, denies the Board power to proceed on a First Schedule matter and misstates the period as 60 days; option 3 misroutes First Schedule matters to the Disciplinary Committee and misnames the appellate forum.
